display.title: The Brachah for Putting Up a Mezuzah
display.summary_short: Every room except the bathroom needs a mezuzah; here is the brachah 'likboa mezuzah' and how and where the mezuzah is affixed.
display.summary_long: A Mitzvah Time lesson from the Tzivos Hashem radio show. Uncle Yossi reviews that every room of the house needs a mezuzah, with one exception: the bathroom or washroom. He then teaches the brachah said before putting up a mezuzah. Like every mitzvah's brachah, it thanks Hashem for the privilege of doing His commandment, and it ends with two special words, 'likboa mezuzah', to affix a mezuzah. The brachah is said right before the mezuzah is put up. The mezuzah goes on the right doorpost, on the upper third, somewhere above your shoulder, tilted toward the room you are entering, and is nailed in place right after the brachah. Uncle Yossi suggests gathering the whole family to watch, so everyone can answer amen and kiss the new mezuzah for the first time.
display.lesson: Make the brachah 'likboa mezuzah' before putting up a mezuzah, and make it a family occasion.
